lines: Morgan Kim
+1 (555) 010-8173 | morgan.kim@example.com | example.com/code/mkim
EDUCATION
Clearwater Institute of Technology | B.S. in Electrical Engineering | Metro City, USA | Sep 2017 - May 2021
EXPERIENCE
Clearwater Sensors | Hardware Test Engineer | Metro City, USA | Apr 2022 - Feb 2023
- Automated end-of-line tests for a humidity sensor, cutting test time per unit from 90 to 25 seconds across 20,000 units a month.
- Traced a batch of early field failures to a solder-paste change; the findings updated the reflow profile and cut returns from 2.1% to 0.4%.
- Wrote the calibration procedure for the sensor line, cutting calibration drift complaints from 15 to 2 a quarter.
- Designed a test fixture that checked 8 boards at once, raising station throughput from 40 to 150 boards an hour.
Voltline Robotics | Embedded Software Engineer | Metro City, USA | Mar 2023 - Jun 2025
- Improved update speed by 60% by compressing firmware images and resuming interrupted downloads.
- Wrote a hardware-in-the-loop test rig that ran 400 motor-control tests on every firmware build.
- Added a crash logger that saved the last 2 seconds of sensor data to flash, which found the root cause of 5 field failures.
- Sampled the motor's 5 kHz vibration signal at 8 kHz so the fault detector could capture it without aliasing.
- Fixed a race condition on the counter shared by the interrupt handler and the main loop by declaring the counter volatile.
- Rewrote the motor-controller firmware for a warehouse robot fleet of 300 units, cutting control-loop jitter from 120 to 15 microseconds and field motor faults by 60%.
PROJECTS
Low-Power Weather Station | Independent Project | C, STM32 | Jan 2025 - Present
- Engineered a next-generation, innovation-driven IoT solution that redefines sustainable environmental sensing.
- Cut average current from 4.2 mA to 0.9 mA by sleeping between readings and batching radio transmissions.
- Published the schematics and firmware openly, and a local school built two stations from them.
Formula Student Electric Car | Electronics Lead, Team of 12 | C | Sep 2019 - May 2021
- Worked on firmware and testing for the robot fleet's motor controllers.
- The CAN-bus firmware for the dashboard was written and tested against the motor controller before each race.
- Rewrote motor-control firmware for a fleet of about 300 robots, cutting control-loop jitter eightfold and motor faults by more than half.
SKILLS
Tools: C, C++, STM32, oscilloscopes
Methods: firmware, hardware-in-the-loop testing, CAN, low-power design

items.says: The experience entries are not in newest-first order.
items.because: Clearwater Sensors appears above the more recent Voltline Robotics role, making the chronology harder to scan.

items.says: Education appears before professional experience.
items.because: Leading with experience would give the reader the most relevant work history sooner.

items.says: The résumé shows a ten-month gap between graduation and the next listed role.
The automation method is unspecified.
The sentence assigns the reflow-profile change to the findings, not to a person.
The strongest result is not the opening bullet.
The calibration reference or control approach is missing.
The 60% improvement does not identify what was measured.
items.because: A reader cannot tell whether it means a shorter update duration, a higher download rate, or another measure.

items.says: The rig’s test volume is given, but its effect is not.
items.because: The workload alone does not show whether the rig caught defects earlier or saved verification time.

items.says: The logger’s role in finding the failures is buried in the trailing clause.
An 8 kHz sampling rate cannot capture a 5 kHz signal without aliasing, and the line states intended capability rather than an achieved outcome.
items.because: The Nyquist frequency is 4 kHz, so the signal will alias.

items.says: Declaring the shared counter volatile does not fix the race condition.
items.because: Volatile does not make counter operations atomic or synchronize the interrupt handler and main loop.

items.says: The line does not name the observable problem or behavior the race-condition fix changed.
items.because: Without a concrete symptom, the value of resolving it remains unclear.

items.says: The fleet description separates the rewrite from its two quantified results.
items.because: The reader encounters the fleet size before the jitter and fault reductions, making the connection less immediate.

items.says: The strongest Voltline bullet is not first in the entry.
items.because: Leading with the firmware rewrite and quantified improvements would show its impact sooner.

items.says: The firmware change is described broadly, without identifying what drove the improvements.
The project description is promotional and does not identify technical work or a concrete result.
items.because: A reader cannot tell what the station senses, what you built, or why the project is valuable.

items.says: The strongest project result is not the opening bullet.
items.because: The quantified current reduction would show the project’s value sooner.

items.says: “Openly” is vague and may repeat the meaning of “Published.”
The first bullet names neither a specific contribution nor an outcome.
items.because: “Worked on firmware and testing” does not show what you did or what changed for the car or team.

items.says: The passive wording hides who wrote and tested the CAN-bus firmware, and the line gives no outcome.
items.because: The reader cannot tell that you performed the work or what it accomplished.

items.says: The fleet-level rewrite and results duplicate the later Voltline claim and conflict with this entry’s dates.
items.because: The Formula Student and Voltline entries place the same achievement in different periods and projects.

items.says: The strongest bullet is not first in the entry.
items.because: Once its project and dates are accurate, leading with its quantified results would show the contribution sooner.

items.says: The line does not identify the technical change behind the reported improvements.
The reduction amounts lack a baseline and measurement context.
items.because: A reader cannot tell what the reductions are compared with, making their size and basis difficult to assess.

items.says: The Formula Student entry’s dashboard and CAN-bus work sits awkwardly beside bullets about a robot fleet.
items.because: They read as contributions to different projects, making it difficult to tell what belongs to the entry.
